static_traits.name: Lin Peini
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends are strained due to excessive spending; has many friends to confide in, but has not yet discussed the financial difficulties with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not previously received treatment or counseling for psychological problems; no similar problems occurred previously
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, good logic, high cooperativeness, able to self-reflect, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I have difficulty managing finances, specifically overspending and impulsive purchases, leading to financial stress and anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realize my excessive spending has led to financial difficulties and affected my overall well-being.
growth_experiences: After starting work and having a higher income, the immediate pleasure brought by shopping gradually reinforced impulsive shopping behavior; when stressed or anxious, the client was more inclined to seek quick relief through shopping, which over time negatively affected savings and triggered higher anxiety and guilt.

core_beliefs: I will never become smart about money management
Only shopping can make me feel better

special_situations.event: On a high work-pressure day, opening an online shopping platform or entering a store after work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel stressed or anxious, shopping is the fastest and most effective way to relieve it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Numbing uncomfortable emotions by purchasing immediately, temporarily gaining comfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Buying something will make me feel a bit better

special_situations.event: When checking bills or realizing savings have decreased
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I overspend the budget once, it means I am not smart and am bad at financial management
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Coping through self-blame and avoidance (not discussing financial predicament with friends)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never become smart about money management

special_situations.event: Recalling moments of having stuck to a budget or found a good deal
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even if there has been success, this does not mean I can continuously manage money well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Denying positive evidence, maintaining negative self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time was just luck; it does not mean I know money management

special_situations.event: When, after making a budget, one fails to stick to it once
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do it completely, it equals total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Giving up continuing to try, returning to the old pattern of shopping to seek comfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I just cannot control my shopping; budgets are useless for me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain emotional comfort and self-mastery (being acknowledged by oneself in money management)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing loss of control will worsen financial pressure, being looked down on by others, and damaged relationships
defense_goal: Quickly relieving inner anxiety and emptiness through shopping
Avoids exposing financial problems to others to evade feelings of shame

object_relations.self_representation: A guilty, out-of-control spender who feels not smart enough
object_relations.object_representation: Others/friends who may judge or not understand oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When realizing they overspent the budget and being advised to discuss the financial predicament with others (such as friends)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences others' attention as judgment, worrying about being looked down on (transference: projecting the anticipated negative evaluation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses a self-blaming tone, frequently saying 'it is all because I am incapable / I should understand finances better', reduces willingness to mention or seek others' support, with a soft tone and avoiding asking for help directly.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores the relationship between emotions and shopping and guides identification of triggers
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to abstract the problem into technical topics of 'strategy / budget', downplaying emotional vulnerability and the experience of shame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Discusses budget steps and data in rational, analytical language, avoiding describing concrete emotional experiences; steady speech rate, rather objective.

manifestations: Having many friends but not discussing financial difficulties
Interpersonal relationships strained by excessive spending
Choosing to shop alone to relieve emotions when under stress
outcomes: Impulsive spending as a substitute way of connecting

manifestations: After income increases, experiencing higher anxiety between choices and responsibilities
Facing conflict between self-decision and restraint (between budget and impulsive shopping)
outcomes: Escaping choice pressure and sense of responsibility through shopping
A sense of financial loss of control and reduced self-efficacy

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses self-blaming statements like 'I should/must understand money management better'
Demanding harshly of oneself by external standards (ought to be able to control spending)

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: When needing help, choosing to endure alone, not discussing financial difficulties with friends
Converting help-seeking energy into self-blame and self-criticism

positive_force: Positive attitude; willing to try recording triggers and behavioral experiments
Able to notice the relationship between shopping and stress, having self-reflection ability
Having non-shopping ways to relax such as reading and walking
Has many friends; potential social support resources exist
negative_force: Using shopping as the main emotion regulation strategy under stress, forming impulsive consumption
Has cognitive biases (Disqualifying the Positive, Fortune Telling, Overgeneralization, All-or-Nothing Thinking)
Strong shame and guilt, hindering seeking help from others
Difficulty maintaining a budget, with repeated failures strengthening self-negation
Lack of self-control after income increases, triggering higher spending

antecedent: Feeling pressure or Anxiety after work
Opening an online shopping platform or entering a store
Increased income makes purchases easier to achieve
target_behavior.core_reason: Uses shopping as a rapid emotion-repair method; low financial-management self-efficacy, accompanied by cognitive biases reinforcing expectations of failure
target_behavior.function: Avoids unwelcome things (stress and anxiety) and obtains immediate pleasure and comfort
target_behavior.consequence: Financial pressure and reduced savings, anxiety and guilt worsen, possibly affecting work performance and straining interpersonal relationships
